actuator_playground_worker.description: Exact-tenant actuator-playground scratch worker. Interactive `pnpm playground` records sessions and ADF drafts under active/shared/tmp/{confidential,personal}/${KYBERION_TENANT}/actuator-playground/. Writes on the tmp floor are admitted by default_allow, but child actuators and session reads need an authorized identity on that partition. This role gives the playground the same effective identity on its own tenant scratch that the claimed-WorkItem path already has — never knowledge/, other tenants, other domains on the tmp floor, staging, cache, or system floors.

archived_mission_state_reader.description: Archived mission state reader (libs/core/foundation/archived-mission-state-capability.ts): read-only, tenant-bound (libs/core/authority.ts TENANT_BOUND_READER_ROLES). libs/core/mission/mission-decision-lock.ts loadDecisionCaseMissionState assumes it to read one archived tenant mission's active/archive/missions/<personal|confidential>/<tenant>/<id>/mission-state.json, always inside an exact read-only capability naming that file (plus product schemas). No write, no other file of the mission folder or archive, no mission lifecycle authority (it replaces the borrowed mission_controller role on that read).

audit_mirror_writer.description: G17 follow-up: dedicated store-writer of the audit chain's per-tenant mirror (active/shared/runtime/audit-mirror/confidential/<tenant>/). libs/core/authority.ts registers it as the audit chain's tenant mirror writer context, always bound to the entry's tenant, so the grant resolves through ${KYBERION_TENANT} to that one tenant's mirror directory. Its only role grant is that write (no role read grant). Like every narrow store-writer role it runs with persona worker, so it also keeps the paths every worker identity has (security-policy default_allow and worker persona grants, e.g. active/shared/tmp/ and the current mission's evidence); it adds nothing else. Nothing else assumes it (resident dots and coordination store writers run as infrastructure_sentinel, which has no audit mirror grant). The legacy-named context also encloses the audit chain own key/lock/master persistence, after the caller tenant and attribution have been checked and captured. Its role policy grants are unchanged: common worker defaults already cover those paths. Persistence runs only canonical audit code and keeps the caller resource-access ceiling; no audit read/key/append authority is added to narrow application store roles.

check_chronos_perf_baseline.description: CE-08: weekly Chronos performance baseline (pnpm kyberion check chronos-perf, schedule ce-chronos-perf). Samples FPS and JS heap of the Chronos UI in a headless browser and writes exactly one report file; it never changes Chronos state.

chronos_gateway.description: Chronos control surface authority for coordination and terminal routing.

chronos_localadmin.description: Chronos local admin authority for deterministic mission, runtime, and surface control from the local control plane.

chronos_mirror_v2.description: Chronos UI mirror authority for interacting with the orchestration system and observability logs.

chronos_operator.description: Chronos operator authority for read-only mission visibility and runtime observability.

chronos_tenant_runner.description: Chronos tenant-scoped pipeline runner. Entered ONLY in the child process chronos spawns for a schedule discovered under knowledge/confidential/{tenant}/pipelines/ (and, in the daemon, synchronously while listing/reading that tenant's pipeline files), always bound to that tenant (KYBERION_TENANT / execution-scope tenant, KYBERION_TENANT_SCOPE_REQUIRED=1 in the child). Grants resolve through ${KYBERION_TENANT}, so reads are limited to the bound tenant's confidential root plus the tenant registry; knowledge landings go through ingest:commit (ingest_commit role); writes are limited to that tenant's audit/trace mirrors.

concierge_management_reader.description: Read-only management projection and fresh owner-membership verification. Requires an exact request resource capability; no write operations or credential access.

concierge_management_writer.description: Authenticated human-owner organization/project descriptive mutation role. Requires a matching immutable request resource capability; exact ceiling precedes all ambient/default grants. No lifecycle, membership, provisioning or deployment authority.

customer_channel_binding_store.description: Customer channel binding storage (libs/core/foundation/customer-channel-binding-store-capability.ts): scripts/customer-channel/bindings.ts writeBindingChange (pnpm kyberion customer-channel bind|unbind) assumes it to read and write one tenant's knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/connections/channel-bindings.json; tenant-bound (libs/core/authority.ts TENANT_BOUND_READER_ROLES). Its grant is the bound tenant's knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/connections/ directory; the tier guard narrows every write and mkdir to the bindings file and the directories leading to it. No connection secrets, no other customer/ file, no knowledge or runtime state (it replaces customer_create on that write).

cyber_security.description: Security review authority for threat modeling, vulnerability analysis, and mission veto power.

daemon_watchdog.description: EV-02: heartbeat watchdog authority. Observes daemon liveness and raises governed recovery wake triggers. Deliberately has no write scope over daemon state or repo config — it reports and requests, it does not reconfigure.

decision_ledger.description: Decision-ledger write authority: appends and promotes decisions under the active tenant's knowledge/confidential/{tenant}/decisions/ and customers/ only.

delegation_record_store.description: Tenant-bound store role of the delegated-task trace and record partitions (libs/core/workforce/delegated-task-observability.ts). The delegation store assumes it (withExecutionContext / withExecutionContextAsync) for every tenant partition read and write — trace append, record write/read/listing, child-inbox queue I/O, background-completion notification queue (libs/core/mission/delegation-notifications.ts: <partition>/notifications.jsonl) append, read and claim — always bound to the delegation's tenant, so the grants resolve through ${KYBERION_TENANT} to that one tenant's active/shared/runtime/delegation-records/confidential/<tenant>/ partition. Tenant-bound (TENANT_BOUND_READER_ROLES): a caller with another active tenant cannot bind it, so a process bound to one tenant never reads another tenant's delegation instructions or results. The inter-process locks stay under the caller's role. No knowledge, mission, system partition, legacy observability or customer/ grant.

deliverable_inbox_writer.description: Deliverable inbox writer (libs/core/foundation/deliverable-inbox-writer-capability.ts): libs/core assumes it only to add an operator task to the deliverable inbox (active/shared/inbox/entries.jsonl, libs/core/task/deliverable-inbox.ts addInboxEntry) on behalf of a caller with no inbox grant: the CD-10 bolt-review rejection (libs/core/mission/mission-bolt-review.ts) and the CD-11 operator hand-off / manual reminder tasks (libs/core/customer-decision/operator-handoff.ts). Its grant is the inbox and the shared lock directory; the tier guard narrows every write and mkdir to the inbox entries file, its directory and the inbox's own deliverable-inbox-<sha256>.lock files. No other active/shared/runtime/ path, no knowledge, mission, approval or surface state.

designer.description: Visual identity and UX authority for interaction design and design-system stewardship.

dot_charter_store.description: Store role of dot charter documents (libs/core/dot/dot-lifecycle.ts): dots/ at repo root, knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/dots/ and knowledge/personal/dots/<owner-hash>/ — all three custodies. The lifecycle facade assumes it (withExecutionContext) at each charter read/write inside the dot_lifecycle_worker process, binding the charter's tenant for confidential custody and explicitly clearing the ambient tenant ('' tenantCleared) for personal and system custody. Its read scopes additionally carry the validation reads that ran under the former dot_lifecycle_writer (tenants/<t>.json, organization operational state, runtime projects). Deliberately not a role a dot may bind at runtime, so an active dot can never rewrite the contract it runs under. The lifecycle audit ledger, activation heartbeats, event-continuation state and inter-process locks live under other roles (dot_lifecycle_runtime_store / the worker's ambient locks grant).

dot_lifecycle_runtime_store.description: Store role of the dot lifecycle runtime surfaces (libs/core/dot/dot-lifecycle.ts): the lifecycle audit ledger (active/shared/runtime/dot-lifecycle-audit.jsonl, append-only), activation heartbeats (active/shared/runtime/heartbeats/) and dot event-continuation state (active/shared/runtime/dot/.../event-continuations/ + events.jsonl). Assumed inside the lifecycle facade for these writes only — charter documents go through dot_charter_store and inter-process locks stay under the dot_lifecycle_worker ambient role. The narrow.only declaration restricts writes to exactly those artifacts and their mkdir ancestors. Tenant-confidential event-continuation partitions bind the charter's tenant; personal and system partitions run with the ambient tenant explicitly cleared. Protected runtime data also requires projected knowledge-tier grants; the raw read/metadata/write/mkdir purpose ceilings forbid using those virtual grants on actual knowledge files. Confidential projection grants expand only from the bound tenant; cleared custody does not admit confidential data.

ecosystem_architect.description: Core architecture and repo evolution authority.

evaluate_model_role_fitness.description: TC-15: role-fitness evaluator authority. Runs the governed model role-fitness probes and appends their verdicts. Its only write scope is that journal — it measures models, it never staffs, dispatches or reconfigures anything.

generation_scheduler.description: EV-01: media-generation schedule daemon authority. Owns the generation schedule registry and its trigger deliveries; deliberately narrower than chronos_gateway, which has no write scope over media-generation state.

infrastructure_sentinel.description: Shared core role assumed internally by coordination store writers (work coordination, peer messaging, mesh, the stimuli journal) and by resident dots whose charters bind it (e.g. repo-guardian). Narrow coordination/observability/runtime write scope only — it reports and delegates, it does not reconfigure.

knowledge_steward.description: Knowledge maintenance authority across governed knowledge trees.

mission_controller.description: Mission lifecycle authority with mission state and observability write access.

nexus_daemon.description: EV-03: KANS nerve daemon authority. Routes stimuli, dispatches terminal work, and raises governed reflex wake triggers. Already declared in security-policy.json for secure-io write scopes; registered here so its reflex triggers carry an authority snapshot the trigger gate can verify (an unregistered role is rejected outright).

notification_preferences_reader.description: Shared operator delivery reader for the single knowledge/personal/notification-preferences.json routing file. Reads validated notification preferences only; no other personal files, writes, or decision authority.

organization_operator.description: Tenant-scoped organization operator role assumed by organization management scripts and resident dots overseeing organization operations, services, and cadences.

peer_responder_reader.description: Least-privilege reader for peer conversation auto replies. libs/core/mesh/peer-auto-reply.ts assumes it, bound to the receiving tenant, to retrieve tenant knowledge (queryTenantKnowledge) that grounds an opt-in LLM reply; it reads that tenant's profile, knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/ only, never knowledge/confidential/<tenant>/connections/ (peer secrets; security-policy.json deny_read), and writes nothing (persona worker). It is a tenant-bound reader (authority.ts TENANT_BOUND_READER_ROLES): the bound tenant must be explicit and equal the caller's active tenant when one exists.

perception_media_worker.description: Shared core exact-tenant media-perception scratch worker. The perception CLI commands (see/listen/watch) normalize media into a scratch dir on the persisted scope's own tier partition — the write side is admitted by the tmp/cache default_allow, but reads on protected tiers need an authorized identity. This role gives the STT/OCR bridge stage and the --index/--search semantic-index stage of that command the same effective identity the claimed-WorkItem path already has: read+write on active/shared/tmp/{confidential,personal}/${KYBERION_TENANT}/ and active/shared/staging/{confidential,personal}/${KYBERION_TENANT}/, plus the semantic index subtree active/shared/cache/{confidential,personal}/${KYBERION_TENANT}/perception/ only (never the rest of the cache floor), bound to the scope's own tenant. It never reads knowledge/, other tenants, other partitions, or system floors.

qa_lead.description: Quality assurance authority for test strategy, coverage validation, and regression evidence.

ruthless_auditor.description: Independent audit authority for evidence inspection, verdict issuance, and mission-halt power.

slack_bridge.description: Slack gateway authority for channel ingress and observability.

software_developer.description: Implementation authority for test and product code paths.

sovereign_concierge.description: Personal onboarding and identity synchronization authority.

surface_runtime.description: Surface runtime authority for reconciling and supervising managed surfaces.

system_configurator.description: Configuration authority for intentional, governed changes to Kyberion's own capabilities. Covers service integration setup, voice engine registration, and tenant bootstrapping. Changes under this role are always executed via a config mission — not ad-hoc.

tenant_approval_partition_index_reader.description: Read-only index reader of the per-tenant approval store partitions (libs/core/governance/approval-store-location.ts listApprovalPartitions). Assumed only by a process without an active tenant to enumerate the tenant directory names under active/shared/runtime/tenant-approvals/<personal|confidential>/; descendant reads are explicitly denied, so it never reads a record. Each listed tenant is then read as the tenant-bound tenant_approval_store. No write authority.

tenant_approval_store.description: Tenant-bound store role of the per-tenant approval store partitions (libs/core/governance/approval-store-location.ts). The approval store assumes it (withExecutionContext) for every tenant partition read and write, always bound to the record's tenant, so the grants resolve through ${KYBERION_TENANT} to that one tenant's active/shared/runtime/tenant-approvals/<personal|confidential>/<tenant>/ partition (public tenant records are stored in the confidential partition): it reads, writes and lists request records, reads and writes passkey challenges and appends the channel's approval event log. Tenant-bound (TENANT_BOUND_READER_ROLES): a caller with another active tenant cannot bind it, so a process bound to one tenant never finds another tenant's approvals. No knowledge, mission, system approval tree or customer/ grant.

tenant_ledger_store.description: D9: tenant-bound store role of the hybrid ledger's tenant partitions (libs/core/governance/ledger.ts). libs/core/governance/ledger.ts assumes it (withExecutionContext) for every tenant partition read and append, always bound to the record's tenant, so the grants resolve through ${KYBERION_TENANT} to that one tenant's active/shared/runtime/tenant-ledger/<personal|confidential>/<tenant>/ partition (public tenant records are stored in the confidential partition): it reads the hash-chain tail, appends tenant records and tenant mission metadata, and verifies the chain. Tenant-bound (TENANT_BOUND_READER_ROLES): a caller with another active tenant cannot bind it. No knowledge, mission, system-ledger or customer/ grant.

tool_runtime_policy_reader.description: Shared tool availability policy reader for the canonical product policy and exact operator or configured customer onboarding policy. Explicit custom paths retain the caller's own permissions. No installation, pinning, writes, or decision authority.

workspace_graph_reader.description: Workspace graph read model (MSN-SURFACE-UNIFY-20261103): read-only join of missions, projects, organizations, work items, approvals, agent identities, tenant profiles and member profiles for libs/core/surface/workspace-graph.ts. It is never tenant-bound: rows are filtered afterwards by the caller's server-resolved SurfaceAuthorizationContext (viewerAdmitsNode), so a client tenant can only narrow. No write grant; persona worker.

workspace_tenant_registry_index_reader.description: Shared core read-only workspace tenant selector index reader. Used only for authenticated viewers whose tenant grants are all. Enumerates registry filenames only; descendant file reads are explicitly denied. Each valid slug is subsequently checked by the exact tenant-bound registry reader; no personal profile fields or write authority are exposed.

workspace_tenant_registry_reader.description: Shared core exact-tenant registry existence reader. Workspace resolution first narrows authenticated viewer grants, then binds this read-only context to that tenant. Reads one knowledge/personal/tenants/${KYBERION_TENANT}.json profile and returns only tenant_slug; never exposes personal profile fields or grants directory enumeration or writes.
